what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee voted unanimously to recommend its ranked list of capital requests to the town manager, with a total as heard in the meeting.
The senior center carpet was dropped from this year's list and can wait until fiscal 27.
The records room was moved above the utility tractor, and the public safety carpet was also moved up.
The committee voted unanimously to restore the police vehicle order, with regular cruisers above the canine cruiser, after the chief's input.
The committee's capital policy recommendation is to raise the capital threshold and extend useful life to five years, to be drafted before the fiscal year ends.

why_it_matters: The ranked list sets which building repairs, vehicles and equipment the town manager is advised to fund first, so it shapes what capital spending reaches Town Meeting and, through borrowing or taxes, the tax bill.

A higher capital threshold would push smaller projects into the facilities budget, which is part of the operating budget and mostly funded by taxes, so some costs would move from capital to operating.
watch_next: Next meeting February 2, with members trying to arrange a joint meeting with the finance committee on the capital policy.
The town manager is to look for unexpected capital that could cover higher town hall and Ritter building costs.
